dominant_strengths: Atmospheric rain streaks layered on deep navy create genuine ambient mood that mirrors the actual weather conveyed
Restrained hierarchy: tracked-out city label, oversized 54°, soft secondary metadata reads instantly without visual noise
Tonal palette is coherent — every text tier sits on a single blue luminance ramp, no clashing accents
dominant_weaknesses: Conceptually safe — yet another temperature card with the rain particle trick, no novel data or interaction layer
Degree symbol sits awkwardly high and detached from the 54, breaking the otherwise careful typographic pairing
Bottom metadata row feels like leftover text dump rather than a composed footer; weak alignment grid with the hero
fix_priorities: Tighten the degree glyph kerning/baseline to the numeral so the hero number reads as one unit
Introduce a second data layer (hourly trend, pressure ribbon) to justify the card's vertical real estate
Differentiate from generic weather widgets via a signature element — typographic mark, condition-driven palette shift, or generative motion
Strengthen footer grid: align Sun 4:47 PM baseline with humidity block on a shared rule
rationale.norman_balance: Strong visceral atmosphere and reflective calm, but behavioral utility is thin — it tells time and temp, nothing actionable.
rationale.intent_fit: Delivers the 'ambient' half of the brief convincingly through mood and restraint, but the 'weather' half is informationally minimal and undifferentiated.
